input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Section 10(a) gives us a broad Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, the Creative, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. Because Kubient's warranties expressly include non-infringement of third-party IP (§9(b)(i): "the Service and any deliverables provided hereunder by Kubient do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party"), data security (§9(b)(iii)) and compliance with Law (§9(b)(v), (ix)), the IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach and misconduct heads of the preferred position are all captured, with no infringement carve-outs. Section 11 supplies the standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition precedent, indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to no admission of liability against us, cooperation at the indemnitor's cost), and §7(a) carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion, so no super-cap constrains recovery. This sits at (indeed above) the preferred position. Two sub-elements short of the ideal are noted but not flagged: our reciprocal indemnity in §10(b) reaches our breach of any representation or warranty and our acts or omissions rather than being confined to Content/Properties and breach of law, and the §10(a)(iii) Creative head is knowledge-qualified. Both are mutual-drafting artefacts that do not defeat the Vendor indemnity rule, and the Customer-side breadth is better addressed under the customer-indemnity rule than by reopening this clause.
